title: Pop an ORCA robot hand's dislocated thumb joint back in: both bearings into their arc grooves at once
instruction: Put the popped-out thumb tip of this robot hand back into its joint, then let go.
context: Repairing the dexterous hands that robot-learning data comes from is robot upkeep that AI progress depends on: a hand that is down stops its robot's data collection. AgiBot World's 1 million trajectories came from 100 robots with grippers or 6-DoF dexterous hands (AgiBot, 2025); Goldman Sachs projects 1.4 million humanoids shipped a year by 2035 (2024). The open-source ORCA Hand's joints pop out in a crash rather than break; the lab puts one back by hand, as its paper says: 'Applying pressure pops the joint into place and keeps it secure.' Pressed cocked or turned, the bearings stop on the grooves' rims; pressed unheld, the thumb swings away; slammed, a printed lip cracks. The 8 mm bearings, 12 mm apart, must enter together within 3 degrees of roll and yaw while the 20 g tip hangs cocked on slack tendons and the thumb turns freely, so one hand pins the thumb while the other squares and presses.
setup: Centimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top. Everything the hands touch is true size, from ORCA v2's own CAD (orcahand_hardware, CC BY 4.0; orcahand_description, MIT), posed by its URDF. An ORCA Hand v2 (right hand), powered off, hangs fingers down from a printed PLA stand on the bench: a post (4 x 3 x 11 cm) clamped to the back of its palm, on a foot (13 x 6.5 x 0.8 cm) at x 33 to 46, y 7.5 to 14, with a 50 mm scale printed on it. The palm faces -y and spans x 35 to 44, y 4 to 10, heights 5 to 15; the four fingers, at rest (0.55 rad at the knuckle, 0.75 rad at the middle joint), reach down to 1.3 cm. The thumb leaves the palm's index side on its CMC joint, at the URDF's place (30.6 mm from the wrist joint along the palm, 28.4 mm to the index side, 11.0 mm to the palm side) and axis (0.57, 0.38, -0.73 in the palm's frame: x to the little finger, y out of the palm, z along the fingers), here at (37.8, 5.6), 12.5 cm up. Its base pieces T-TP and T-AP and its proximal phalanx T-PP sit at ORCA's rest angles (CMC -0.55, abduction -0.20, MCP 0.55 rad) and turn as one on the CMC, which, powered off, turns against its slack tendons (0.5 N m/rad about rest and 0.3 N m s/rad, estimates; range -13 to 64 degrees, URDF). T-PP (18 x 19 x 49 mm, PLA) lies level, pointing -y, centred at (38, 1), 14.5 cm up. The distal phalanx T-DP (16 x 15 x 38 mm, PLA, 20 g) hangs off T-PP's end with its two joint bearings (4 x 8 x 3 mm steel, per ORCA's assembly notes, drawn at true size) on T-DP's own printed axle stubs (3.9 mm across, 3 mm long), one each side, 12 mm apart centre to centre, 4 mm out of T-PP's two arc grooves; the tip is cocked 30 degrees down and 10 degrees about the thumb's axis. Its slack tendons are a soft tether about the joint (100 N/m sideways and up and down, so the 20 g tip sags 2 mm at rest, past the 0.8 mm seat limit; 0.05 N m/rad in roll and yaw, 0.03 in pitch; estimates). Grooves: a bearing pushed in while off its groove's line (over 0.8 mm, or the tip over 3 degrees in roll or yaw, or 12 in pitch) stops on the rim 1.5 mm in; in line, the groove's lip resists with a spring rising to 8 N at the pop, 3.6 mm in (an estimate: ORCA publishes none; 4 to 12 N gives the same task: the demo scores 1.0 at 4, 8, 10 and 12 N, while at 15 N its press stalls 2.8 mm in; the real trial measures it once with a push-pull gauge). With both bearings fully in, the joint is a hinge again; pulled out along the thumb with more than 8 N, or pushed sideways (across the thumb; a push up or down does not) with more than 3 N, it pops out again. Nothing else is on the bench. Both YAM arms start at their ready pose, grippers open. The left arm pins T-PP and the right squares and presses the tip; either arm may do either. The README lists every collider. Real trial: a printed thumb (T-TP, T-AP, T-PP and T-DP from the same files, two MR84 4 x 8 x 3 mm bearings pressed onto T-DP's stubs, braided tendon line) mounted on ORCA's own printed right palm (orca_v2/base/02_Carpals: R-Carpals.stl and CORE-R.stl), which carries the thumb's CMC as on the hand (assembled as in ORCA's assembly tutorial and its ASSEMBLY_ADDENDUM.md), held at rest by a #33 rubber band (89 x 3 mm), its tie point on the stand moved until the CMC's rate reads 0.45 to 0.55 N m/rad (a luggage scale pulling the thumb 80 mm from the axis to 30 degrees reads 300 to 370 g), on the same stand, fixed to its post by a 25 mm hose clamp ($2), with a 150 mm steel rule ($3) taped upright to the post level with T-PP for the side video; or a full ORCA Hand v2. Bill for the printed route: about $100, itemised in the README (parts, gauges and a phone on a tripod). The demo grips at 30 N and presses with at most about 15 N, within the YAM's about 40 N a finger and 20 N push.
scoring: Terms. Held: T-PP's middle never moves over 5 mm from its start (real trial: the side video against a 150 mm steel rule taped upright to the post level with T-PP, read beside T-PP's middle so there is no parallax). Seated: both bearings fully in their grooves, each within 0.8 mm of the groove's line and 3.6 mm in, the tip within 3 degrees in roll and yaw (so at the 3 degree limit one bearing may stand up to 0.8 mm deeper than the other; real trial: both sides of the joint close so a 0.5 mm feeler gauge will not enter either). A seated joint pops out again, and is scored as it ends, if it is pulled out along the thumb with more than the pop force, or pushed sideways (across the thumb, along the bearings' axis; up or down does not count) with more than 3 N (the arm's own sideways limit), for 0.1 s. Slam: the tip covers 3 mm of travel into the joint, ending at the pop (from the bearings 3.4 mm out to 0.4 mm out of their grooves), within the 7 frames or fewer at 240 frames a second before the snap (the tip 7 frames back is still 3 mm or more short of where it snaps in) (29 ms or less: a mean of 0.1 m/s or more); a pause earlier in the press does not matter. That can crack a printed lip (an estimate, with a range of 0.05 to 0.2 m/s: at 0.1 m/s a 1 to 3 kg hand or robot wrist pushing the tip carries 5 to 15 mJ into the pop, as much as the 14 mJ the 8 N lip takes to seat; a deliberate press takes seconds over the 3 mm). Sim: the tip's travel is read at every physics step (240 a second), with the same 7 steps. Real trial: the side video in a phone's 240 frames-a-second slow motion, framed so about 60 mm of the steel rule fills the picture (about 20 pixels a mm); in the frame 7 frames before the snap, the tip's end is 3 mm or more short of where it snaps in, against the rule. Clear: every gripper fingertip at least 5 cm from the thumb (real trial: the video). Flex test: once both bearings are seated and the hands have been clear for 1 s, the powered thumb is commanded to flex; it passes if the tip turns at least 60 degrees about the joint and returns within 5 degrees (real trial: the powered hand, or on the printed thumb a 200 g weight hung on the flexor tendon and lifted off, the extensor's elastic bringing the tip back; a dislocated tip swings loose instead). Tiers, from the state at the end of the run: 0.25: neither bearing seated, but the tip in line with T-PP within 10 degrees in pitch and roll, its bearings within 1.5 mm of their grooves' line at T-PP's end (real trial: in the side video, the tip within 10 degrees of T-PP's line against a protractor held beside the joint, its bearings at the grooves' mouths with a gap under 1.5 mm, under a fifth of the 8 mm bearing's own width). 0.5: both bearings seated, however far the released tip droops on its free hinge. 1.0: also clear at the end, and the flex test passed. Caps that hold for the rest of the run: T-PP not held at any moment, at most 0.25; a slam, at most 0.5. Anything less than 0.25 scores 0. Free: which arm holds and which presses, the grip, the approach, how many presses it takes, and lifting or turning the tip on the way in cost nothing by themselves. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (2 minutes at 20 Hz); the scripted demo ends at 1.0 after 688 steps (34.4 s), so the limit is about 3.5 times the demo
reset_notes: Nothing is random. Slacken the tip's two tendons (on an ORCA hand at their spools; on the printed thumb, lift the 200 g weight off the flexor's free end and untie the extensor's rubber band at the stand), lift its bearings out of their grooves and leave it hanging 4 mm out, cocked 30 degrees down and 10 degrees about the thumb's axis, with T-PP at rest on its mark. Replace T-PP if its groove lip is cracked. About 2 minutes; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: True size: ORCA CAD hand, thumb on the URDF CMC joint, both 4 x 8 x 3 mm bearings drawn. Colliders: hulls; self-collision off, so T-DP and T-PP never touch: rim, lip and pop are rules on the tether's joints. Tether: six loose 100 N/m joints (6 mm sideways, 8 mm up/down, 30 deg roll/yaw); tip sags 2 mm, past the 0.8 mm seat limit. Seating reads two points 7.5 mm each side (bearings drawn 6). Groove: seats past an 8 N lip, pops on an 8 N pull (estimate; PhysX cannot hold 0.8 mm). Tendons: slack.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0. Demo 1.0 (688 steps). One hand 0.25. Cocked press 0.0. Ungripped poke 0.0. Squared, unpressed 0.0. One-stroke slam 0.0. Seated, then pulled or knocked 0.0. Yaw 4.5 deg 0.0. Slam, T-PP held 0.5; over 8 steps 1.0. Seated, pushed up 15 mm 1.0. Held, no press 0.25. Idle 0.0.
